playbooks.title: Bluetooth dongle fails or conflicts
playbooks.summary: Two Bluetooth radios (onboard + USB dongle) often fight. Windows only wants one stack.
steps: Note whether mouse/headset use onboard BT or a dongle.
Unplug the USB Bluetooth dongle and reboot once — see if onboard BT works alone.
If you need the dongle, disable onboard Bluetooth in Device Manager (Network adapters / Bluetooth), then plug the dongle back in.
Avoid USB 3.0 interference: try a USB 2.0 rear port for the dongle.
Check Event Viewer theme USB / search Bluetooth.
playbooks.whenToStop: If both radios fail after clean disable, stop and check the dongle on another PC.
playbooks.searchQueryTemplate: "{board}" USB Bluetooth failed to start Windows 11 dongle vs onboard

playbooks.title: Disk retries / portable SSD hiccups
playbooks.summary: Windows had to retry a drive — common on USB SSDs with weak cables, power, or failing media.
steps: Identify which drive from Event Viewer / Disk Management (portable vs internal).
If portable: reseat cable, try a rear USB 3.x or Thunderbolt port (not a front hub).
Copy critical data off the drive before more stress tests.
Check free space on the system drive — full disks cause their own chaos.
For internal NVMe: note temperatures and firmware; avoid interrupting large transfers.
playbooks.whenToStop: If SMART warns or retries continue after cable/port change, replace the drive — do not keep writing important data to it.
playbooks.searchQueryTemplate: {disk} disk retry error Windows 11 "reset to device"

playbooks.title: Ethernet link drops and returns
playbooks.summary: Cable link went down/up. Often cable, switch, power saving, or NIC driver — not always the motherboard.
steps: Reseat the Ethernet cable at PC and switch/router.
Try a known-good Cat5e/Cat6 cable.
In Windows power settings, disable USB selective suspend experiments only if Wi‑Fi dongles also act up; for NIC, check adapter Power Management → uncheck 'allow computer to turn off this device'.
Update Intel LAN driver from ASUS board support page (not random third-party packs).
See Event Viewer ethernet-link theme for frequency.
playbooks.whenToStop: If only one wall jack or switch port fails with multiple cables, fix networking gear first.

playbooks.title: GPU driver timeout / black screen recovery
playbooks.summary: Display driver stopped responding and recovered. Care if you saw black screens or hard freezes mid-game.
steps: Note whether it happens in one game, any 3D app, or idle desktop.
Update GPU drivers cleanly (NVIDIA/AMD clean install or DDU if comfortable).
Check GPU power cables and case airflow/temps.
Undervolt or reset GPU overclock / manufacturer OC BIOS to defaults.
Review Event Viewer GPU theme for timing.
playbooks.whenToStop: If black screens continue after clean drivers and stock clocks, stop overclocking and RMA path may be next.

playbooks.title: Sustained high CPU
playbooks.summary: CPU pegged high while you expect the PC to be idle — find the process before assuming hardware fault.
steps: Open Task Manager sorted by CPU — note the top process name.
If Windows Update / antivirus / indexer: wait or reschedule; do not kill critical system processes.
If unknown EXE: note path, disconnect network if suspicious, scan with Malware Defender.
Check temps if the PC is loud/hot under idle load.
playbooks.whenToStop: If an unknown process returns after kill and scan is clean, research the file hash before deleting system files.

playbooks.title: System drive almost full
playbooks.summary: Low free space breaks updates, temp files, and browser caches.
steps: Open Disk Analyzer — clear Downloads, old ISOs, and recycle bin.
Run Storage Sense or Disk Cleanup for Windows Update leftovers.
Move large media libraries to another drive.
Leave at least 20–40 GB free on C: for comfort.
playbooks.whenToStop: If C: is a small SSD and stays full, plan a larger boot drive — do not delete unknown Windows folders.
playbooks.searchQueryTemplate: Windows 11 free up disk space safely C drive full
